p.src: Now Yan Pu was urging Zhang Lu not to aid Liu Zhang when Ma Chao stepped forward and said, “I am deeply grateful for my lord’s kindness, yet have had no way to repay it. Let me lead an army to seize Jiameng Pass and capture Liu Bei alive. I shall compel Liu Zhang to cede twenty prefectures and return them to my lord.” Zhang Lu was delighted. He first sent Huang Quan back by a minor road, then immediately assigned twenty thousand troops to Ma Chao. At the time, Pang De was bedridden with illness and unable to travel, so he remained in Hanzhong. Zhang Lu appointed Yang Bai as army supervisor. Ma Chao and his younger kinsman Ma Dai chose an auspicious day and set out.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xuande’s army was stationed at Luo Castle. The messenger whom Fa Zheng had sent with a letter returned and reported, “Zheng Du has advised Liu Zhang to burn all the grain in the fields and every granary, move the people of Baxi west of the Fu River, and dig deep trenches and raise high ramparts while refusing battle.” When Xuande and Kongming heard this, they were both alarmed. “If he follows that advice, our position will be perilous!” they exclaimed. Fa Zheng laughed. “Do not worry, my lord. Poisonous though the scheme is, Liu Zhang will certainly be unable to adopt it.” Within a few days, word arrived that Liu Zhang had refused to move the people and had rejected Zheng Du’s advice. Only when Xuande heard this was his mind set at ease. Kongming said, “We must advance swiftly and take Mianzhu. Once that place is ours, Chengdu will be easy to capture.” He accordingly sent Huang Zhong and Wei Yan ahead with their troops. Learning that Xuande’s army was approaching, Fei Guan sent Li Yan out to meet it. Li Yan led out three thousand troops, and both sides completed their formations. Huang Zhong rode forth and fought Li Yan for forty or fifty bouts, with neither gaining the advantage. From within the formation Kongming ordered the gong sounded to recall the troops. Huang Zhong returned and asked, “I was just about to capture Li Yan. Why did the military adviser recall me?” Kongming replied, “I have now seen Li Yan’s martial skill. He cannot be taken by force. When you fight again tomorrow, feign defeat and lure him into the valley; then defeat him with an ambush.”

p.src: Huang Zhong accepted the plan. The next day Li Yan again led out his troops. Huang Zhong rode forth once more, but before ten bouts had passed he feigned defeat and fled with his men. Li Yan pursued and was gradually drawn into the valley, where realization suddenly struck him. Just as he hurried to turn back, Wei Yan appeared ahead with his troops drawn up. Kongming himself stood atop the hill and called, “If you will not surrender, strong crossbows lie in ambush on both sides, ready to avenge my Pang Shiyuan!” Li Yan hastily dismounted, removed his armor, and surrendered; not one of his soldiers was harmed. Kongming brought Li Yan before Xuande, who treated him with great generosity. Li Yan said, “Though Fei Guan is related by marriage to the lord of Yizhou, he and I are very close. I shall go and persuade him.” Xuande immediately ordered Li Yan to return to the city and induce Fei Guan to surrender.

p.src: Li Yan entered Mianzhu and extolled Xuande’s benevolence and virtue to Fei Guan; if he did not surrender now, he warned, disaster would surely follow. Fei Guan followed his advice, opened the gates, and surrendered. Xuande then entered Mianzhu and conferred with his officers about dividing the army to take Chengdu. Suddenly an express courier galloped in with an urgent report: “Meng Da and Huo Jun are defending Jiaming Pass, but Zhang Lu of Dongchuan has sent Ma Chao, Yang Bai, and Ma Dai to lead an intense attack upon it. If aid comes late, the pass will be lost.” Xuande was greatly alarmed. Kongming said, “Only Generals Zhang and Zhao are capable of facing him.” Xuande said, “Zilong is still away leading troops and has not returned. Yide is already here; we can send him at once.” Kongming said, “My lord, say nothing for the moment. Allow me to provoke him.”

p.src: Now when Zhang Fei heard that Ma Chao was attacking the pass, he rushed in shouting, “I shall take leave of my elder brother and go fight Ma Chao at once!” Pretending not to hear him, Kongming said to Xuande, “Ma Chao is now attacking the pass, and no one here can match him; only by fetching Guan Yunchang from Jingzhou can we hope to oppose him.” Zhang Fei said, “Why does the military adviser think so little of me? I once stood alone against Cao Cao’s million-man army. Why should I fear a mere Ma Chao?” Kongming replied, “Yide held the bridge over the river and broke its span only because Cao Cao did not know the true state of affairs. Had he known the truth, could the general have emerged unharmed? Ma Chao’s valor is now known throughout the realm. In the great battle at the Wei Bridge, he forced Cao Cao to cut off his beard and cast away his robe, nearly taking his life. He is no ordinary opponent; even Yunchang might not defeat him.” Zhang Fei said, “I shall leave this very moment; if I cannot defeat Ma Chao, I will willingly submit to military punishment!” Kongming said, “If you are willing to put that pledge in writing, you may serve as the vanguard. I ask my lord to make the journey in person. I shall remain to guard Mianzhu. When Zilong returns, I shall decide what is to be done next.” Wei Yan said, “I too am willing to go.”

p.src: Kongming ordered Wei Yan to ride ahead with five hundred scouts, followed by Zhang Fei, while Xuande brought up the rear, and they advanced toward Jiaming Pass. Wei Yan’s scouts arrived below the pass first and encountered Yang Bai. Wei Yan fought Yang Bai, and before ten bouts had passed, Yang Bai fled in defeat. Eager to steal the first victory from Zhang Fei, Wei Yan pressed his advantage and pursued. Ahead, another force stood arrayed, led by Ma Dai. Wei Yan assumed he was Ma Chao and charged to meet him, brandishing his saber and spurring his horse. He fought Ma Dai for fewer than ten bouts, whereupon Ma Dai fled in defeat. Wei Yan gave chase, but Ma Dai turned in the saddle and loosed an arrow that struck Wei Yan’s left arm. Wei Yan hurriedly wheeled his horse and fled. Ma Dai pursued him to the front of the pass, where he saw a general with a voice like thunder gallop down from the ramparts and charge straight toward him. It was Zhang Fei, who had just reached the pass. Hearing the fighting below, he came to look and saw Wei Yan struck by the arrow; he therefore galloped down from the pass and rescued him.

p.src: Zhang Fei shouted at Ma Dai, “Who are you? State your name before we fight!” Ma Dai replied, “I am Ma Dai of Xiliang.” Zhang Fei said, “So you are not Ma Chao! Go back at once! You are no match for me! Send that scoundrel Ma Chao himself! Tell him Zhang Yide of Yan is here!” Ma Dai was furious. “How dare you belittle me!” he cried. Leveling his spear and spurring his horse, he charged straight at Zhang Fei. Before ten bouts had passed, Ma Dai fled in defeat. Zhang Fei was about to pursue when a rider came from the pass and called, “Brother, do not pursue him!” Zhang Fei looked back and saw that Xuande had arrived. He therefore abandoned the pursuit, and they ascended the pass together. Xuande said, “I feared your impetuous temper, so I hurried after you and came here. Now that you have defeated Ma Dai, rest here tonight and fight Ma Chao tomorrow.”

p.src: At daybreak the next morning, drums thundered below the pass as Ma Chao’s army arrived. Looking down from the pass, Xuande saw Ma Chao ride out from among the gate banners, spear in hand; he wore a lion-crested helmet, a beast-faced belt, silver armor, and a white robe; his attire was extraordinary, and his looks were outstanding. Xuande sighed in admiration. “Men call him ‘Ma Chao the Splendid,’ and the name is no empty boast!” Zhang Fei immediately made to descend from the pass. Xuande hastily stopped him. “Do not go out to fight yet. We must first let the edge of his vigor wear away.” Below the pass, Ma Chao challenged Zhang Fei by name to come out and fight. Above, Zhang Fei was so enraged he could have swallowed Ma Chao whole, but three or five times Xuande held him back. When afternoon was drawing on, Xuande saw that the men and horses in Ma Chao’s ranks were all weary. He therefore selected five hundred horsemen and followed Zhang Fei in a charge down from the pass. Seeing Zhang Fei’s force approach, Ma Chao swept his spear backward as a signal and withdrew his troops about a bowshot. Zhang Fei’s soldiers and horses halted together; the troops from the pass continued to file out. Zhang Fei rode forth with his spear leveled and roared, “Do you know Zhang Yide of Yan?” Ma Chao replied, “My family has been ennobled for generations. How should I know some rustic boor?” Zhang Fei flew into a rage. Both horses charged together, and both spears rose as one. They fought for more than a hundred bouts, with neither able to prevail. Watching them, Xuande sighed, “A true tiger of a general!” Fearing that Zhang Fei might come to harm, he urgently ordered the gong sounded to recall the troops. The two generals each returned to their own lines.

p.src: Both armies raised their battle cries and lit a thousand torches, making the field as bright as day. The two generals once again fought fiercely before the lines. After more than twenty bouts, Ma Chao wheeled his horse and fled. Zhang Fei shouted, “Where do you think you are going?” In truth, seeing that he could not overcome Zhang Fei, Ma Chao had devised a stratagem. Feigning defeat, he lured Zhang Fei into pursuit, secretly drew a bronze mace, twisted around, took aim, and hurled it at him. When Zhang Fei saw Ma Chao flee, he was already on his guard. As the bronze mace came flying, Zhang Fei dodged, and it passed beside his ear. As Zhang Fei reined about, Ma Chao came pursuing him in turn. Zhang Fei checked his horse, took up his bow, fitted an arrow, and shot back at Ma Chao. Ma Chao dodged the arrow, and the two generals each returned to his own lines. From before his lines Xuande called out, “I treat men with benevolence and righteousness and do not resort to deceit. Ma Mengqi, withdraw your troops and rest. I shall not take advantage of the moment to pursue you.” Hearing this, Ma Chao personally guarded the rear while his troops gradually withdrew. Xuande likewise recalled his army and returned to the pass.

p.src: The next day, Zhang Fei again wished to descend from the pass and fight Ma Chao. Then word came that the military adviser had arrived. Xuande went to receive Kongming. Kongming said, “I have heard that Mengqi is one of the tiger generals of our age. If he fights Yide to the death, one of them is certain to be injured. A small stratagem can be used to make Ma Chao submit to you, my lord.” Xuande said, “I have seen Ma Chao's valor and greatly admire him. How may I win him?” Kongming replied, “I hear that Zhang Lu of Dongchuan wishes to proclaim himself ‘King of Hanning.’ His adviser Yang Song is exceedingly greedy for bribes. We can send someone by the minor paths straight to Hanzhong, first winning Yang Song over with gold and silver, and then presenting Zhang Lu with a letter saying: ‘I contend with Liu Zhang for Xichuan in order to avenge you. You must not believe words intended to sow discord. Once the affair is settled, I shall sponsor you as King of Hanning.’ This will make him recall Ma Chao's troops. When his order of recall arrives, we can use another stratagem to induce Ma Chao to surrender.”

Sun Qian sought an audience with Yang Song, explained the matter, and presented the treasure. Yang Song was overjoyed. He first took Sun Qian to see Zhang Lu and spoke persuasively on his behalf. If you fail in these three tasks, you may present your own head.’ On the other hand, order Zhang Wei to muster troops and guard the passes against a mutiny by Ma Chao.”

Zhang Wei therefore divided his forces into seven columns and firmly guarded the strategic passes, refusing entry to Ma Chao's army.
Unable either to advance or retreat, Ma Chao could devise no course of action.
Kongming said to Xuande, “Ma Chao is now caught between advance and retreat. Relying on my persuasive tongue, I shall go personally to his camp and convince him to surrender.”
Xuande said, “You, Master, are my right arm and trusted heart. What should I do if some mishap befell you?”
Kongming remained determined to go.
Xuande repeatedly refused to let him depart.

p.src: While they were still deliberating, a sudden report came that Zhao Yun had sent a letter recommending a man from Xichuan who had come to submit. Xuande summoned the man and questioned him. Since he could not employ my counsel, I knew that he was certain to fail. Now, General, your benevolence and virtue are renowned throughout Shu. Knowing that your enterprise will surely succeed, I have therefore come to join you.” Xuande said, “Your coming here, Master, will surely be of benefit to Liu Bei.” Li Hui replied, “I hear that Ma Chao is now caught between advance and retreat. p.src: When Li Hui reached Ma Chao's camp, he first sent a man ahead to announce his name. Ma Chao said, “I know that Li Hui is a persuasive speaker. He must have come to talk me over.” He first had twenty axemen hide below the tent and ordered them, “When I tell you to strike, hack him to mincemeat!” Presently, Li Hui strode proudly inside. Ma Chao sat motionless in the center of the tent and barked at him, “Why have you come?” Li Hui replied, “I have come expressly as a persuader.” Ma Chao said, “The precious sword in my case has just been sharpened. Try saying your piece. If your words make no sense, I shall ask you to try its edge!” Li Hui laughed and said, “Your calamity is not far off, General! I fear only that your newly sharpened sword will not get to try my head, but will instead be tried upon yourself!” Ma Chao asked, “What calamity do I face?” Li Hui said, “I have heard that no skilled detractor could conceal the beauty of Xi Shi of Yue, while no skilled flatterer could hide the ugliness of Wuyan of Qi. ‘At noon the sun begins to decline; when full, the moon begins to wane.’ This is a constant principle under Heaven. Now you bear Cao Cao a blood feud for killing your father, while the people of Longxi harbor bitter hatred against you. Earlier you failed to save Liu Zhang by driving back the army from Jingzhou; afterward you failed to master Yang Song and regain Zhang Lu's favor. At present there is no place for you within the four seas, and you stand alone without a lord. If you should suffer another defeat like that at the Wei Bridge or another loss like that of Ji, how could you show your face before the people of the world?” Ma Chao bowed his head to the ground and said, “Your words are excellent, sir, but I have no path left to take.” Li Hui said, “Since you have accepted my counsel, sir, why are axemen lying in ambush outside the tent?” Deeply ashamed, Ma Chao ordered them all away. Li Hui said, “Imperial Uncle Liu honors the worthy and humbles himself before men of ability. I knew he was certain to succeed, and so I left Liu Zhang and joined him. Your honored father once pledged with the Imperial Uncle to fight the traitor together. Why do you not forsake darkness for light, avenging your father above and winning merit and renown below?” Ma Chao was overjoyed. He immediately summoned Yang Bo, cut him down with one stroke, and carried his head with Li Hui to the pass to surrender to Xuande. Xuande personally welcomed him and treated him with the courtesies due an honored guest. Ma Chao bowed his head and said, “Now that I have met an enlightened lord, it is as though the clouds and mist have parted to reveal the blue sky!”

p.src: By then, Sun Qian had returned. Xuande again ordered Huo Jun and Meng Da to guard the pass, then withdrew his army and advanced upon Chengdu. Zhao Yun and Huang Zhong received him into Mianzhu. A report came: “The Shu generals Liu Jun and Ma Han are approaching with an army.” Zhao Yun said, “I volunteer to go and capture those two!” With that, he mounted his horse and led his troops out. Xuande entertained Ma Chao with wine atop the city wall. Before they had even settled at the table, Zilong had already beheaded both men and presented their heads before the banquet. Even Ma Chao was astonished and respected him all the more. Ma Chao said, “There is no need for my lord to fight. I shall personally summon Liu Zhang out to surrender. If he refuses, my brother Ma Dai and I shall take Chengdu ourselves and present it to you with both hands.” Xuande was delighted. That day, they made merry to their hearts’ content.

p.src: Meanwhile, the defeated soldiers returned to Yizhou and reported to Liu Zhang. Liu Zhang was greatly alarmed and shut himself indoors. When word came that Ma Chao's relief force had reached the north of the city, Liu Zhang at last dared ascend the wall to look. He saw Ma Chao and Ma Dai standing below the wall and shouting, “We ask Liu Jiyu to come speak with us!” Liu Zhang questioned them from atop the wall. Pointing his whip from horseback, Ma Chao said, “I originally led Zhang Lu's troops here to rescue Yizhou, but Zhang Lu listened to Yang Song's slanders and instead sought to harm me. I have now submitted to Imperial Uncle Liu. You should receive his officers and submit, thereby sparing the people from suffering. If you persist in your delusion, I shall be the first to storm the city!” Liu Zhang's face turned ashen with terror, and he fainted upon the wall. The officials revived him. Liu Zhang said, “I was unenlightened, but it is too late for regrets! Better to open the gates and surrender, and thereby save all the people in the city.” Dong He said, “There are still more than thirty thousand troops in the city, and our money, silks, provisions, and fodder can sustain us for a year. Why surrender at once?” Liu Zhang said, “My father and I have been in Shu for more than twenty years, yet we have bestowed no benevolence upon its people. For three years we have waged war, and flesh and blood have been cast upon the fields—all this is my crime. How could my heart be at peace? Better that I surrender and bring peace to the people.”

p.src: When the others heard this, they all shed tears. Suddenly, one man stepped forward and said, “My lord's words accord perfectly with the will of Heaven.” They looked and saw that he was a native of Xichongguo in Baxi. His surname was Qiao, his given name Zhou, and his style Yunnan. He had long been versed in astronomy. Liu Zhang questioned him, and Qiao Zhou said, “One night, while observing the heavens, I saw a host of stars gather over Shu Commandery. The great star among them shone as brightly as the full moon: it was the sign of an emperor. Moreover, a year ago children sang: ‘If you wish to eat the new rice, you must wait until the Former Lord arrives.’ This was a prophecy. The Way of Heaven must not be defied.” Huang Quan and Liu Ba were both enraged at these words and wished to behead him, but Liu Zhang stopped them. Suddenly came a report: “Xu Jing, the governor of Shu Commandery, has climbed over the wall and gone out to surrender.” Liu Zhang returned to his residence weeping bitterly.

p.src: The next day, it was reported that Imperial Uncle Liu had sent his retainer Jian Yong, who was below the wall calling for the gate to be opened. Liu Zhang ordered the gate opened and had him admitted. Jian Yong remained seated in his carriage, gazing about with composed arrogance. Suddenly, a man drew his sword and shouted, “A petty fellow, puffed up by success, who acts as though no one else exists! How dare you disdain the men of ability in our Shu!” Jian Yong hurriedly descended from the carriage to greet him. This man was a native of Mianzhu in Guanghan. His surname was Qin, his given name Mi, and his style Zichi. Jian Yong smiled and said, “I did not recognize you, worthy brother. I hope you will not blame me.” They then went in together to see Liu Zhang, and Jian Yong fully explained Xuande's generosity and magnanimity, assuring him that Xuande had no intention of harming him. Liu Zhang then resolved to surrender and treated Jian Yong with great honor. p.src: Xuande followed his advice and held a grand banquet. More than sixty other surrendered civil and military officers—including Wu Yi, Fei Guan, Peng Yang, Zhuo Ying, Li Yan, Wu Lan, Lei Tong, Li Hui, Zhang Yi, Qin Mi, Qiao Zhou, Lü Yi, Huo Jun, Deng Zhi, Yang Hong, Zhou Qun, Fei Yi, Fei Shi, and Meng Da—were likewise promoted and employed. Zhuge Liang became military adviser; Guan Yunchang, General Who Sweeps Away Rebels and Marquis of Hanshou Village; Zhang Fei, General Who Campaigns Afar and Marquis of Xinting; Zhao Yun, General Who Pacifies Distant Lands; Huang Zhong, General Who Campaigns in the West; Wei Yan, General Who Exalts Martial Might; and Ma Chao, General Who Pacifies the West. Sun Qian, Jian Yong, Mi Zhu, Mi Fang, Liu Feng, Wu Ban, Guan Ping, Zhou Cang, Liao Hua, Ma Liang, Ma Su, Jiang Wan, Yi Ji, and all the former civil and military officers of Jing and Xiang were promoted and rewarded. Soldiers and civilians alike rejoiced.

p.src: Once Yi Province was pacified, Xuande wished to divide the renowned fields and residences of Chengdu among his officers. They should not be seized for private rewards.” Xuande was delighted and accepted his counsel, then instructed Military Adviser Zhuge to draw up the laws for governing the realm. The penal laws were rather severe. Fa Zheng said: “In former times, Emperor Gaozu established only three articles of law, and all the common people were grateful for his virtue. I pray that you, Military Adviser, lighten the punishments and simplify the laws, thereby satisfying the hopes of the people.” Kongming replied: “You understand one side of the matter but not the other. The Qin enforced its laws with savage cruelty, and all the people resented it; therefore Gaozu won the realm through leniency and benevolence. But Liu Zhang was benighted and weak: virtuous government went unpracticed, while authority and punishment commanded no respect. Thus the proper relations between ruler and subject gradually declined. Men were indulged with office, and once they reached the highest station, no further favor remained to bestow. They were accommodated with favors, and once those favors were exhausted, they grew insolent. The abuses that arose stemmed precisely from this. Now I shall inspire awe through the law; when the law is enforced, men will recognize benevolence. I shall limit them through rank; when rank is conferred, they will recognize honor. When benevolence and honor are applied together, superiors and inferiors alike will observe proper bounds. Herein lies the true way of government.” Fa Zheng bowed in submission. From that time onward, soldiers and civilians lived in peace. Troops were divided among the forty-one prefectures to garrison and pacify them, and all were brought under control. As Administrator of Shu Commandery, Fa Zheng repaid every kindness, even the gift of a single meal, and avenged every grudge, even the slightest glare. Only with Xiaozhi's support could he suddenly spread his wings and soar beyond all restraint. How, then, can we now forbid Xiaozhi from acting upon his wishes even a little?” Thus he made no inquiry into the matter. When Fa Zheng heard of this, he too restrained himself.
